findings.summary: THE COUNT WENT STALE AGAIN, INSIDE THE COMMIT THAT RETIRES COUNTING: the closing sentence says 'TWO of these duplicate' over a list of THREE duplicating bullets, and it contradicts IdempotencyWindow.java:43 -- 'THREE of which DUPLICATE' -- staged in the same commit
findings.detail: The DUPLICATED list at Sequencer.java:110-137 now has three <li> entries: a superseded incarnation (:111), a bare v0 slot (:115) and a pod absent from an intermediate checkpoint's pods map (:125, the fifth limit added this round). The closing paragraph at :139-143 still reads 'it is not "answered or refused" either: TWO of these duplicate'. Measured, not inferred: `grep -c '<li>'` over :110-137 is 3, and the same-commit sentence at IdempotencyWindow.java:43 says 'WITH THE LIMITS {@link Sequencer} ENUMERATES -- THREE of which DUPLICATE rather than refuse'. So the staged bytes contain two `src/main` statements of the same property disagreeing (2 against 3) -- which is verbatim the condition the commit's own recorded reason says this row exists to end ('two statements of the same property disagreeing is what this row exists to end') and the fourth recurrence of the defect the row was opened for ('one' M5.25, 'two' M5.27, three at round 1, and now two-vs-three in one commit). Concrete failure scenario, which is the same one the row records for M5.25's sentence: a reader plans a rolling deploy, reaches the summary paragraph -- the last thing in the section and the sentence written to be the takeaway -- counts two duplicating cases, checks that neither applies (no pod restart, no v0 checkpoint in retention), and ships; the third case, the one that needs only two takeovers, is the one the summary just told them was not there. It is also the most reachable of the three, which the bullet itself states. ⚠️ SECOND-ORDER, AND WORTH A SENTENCE IN THE FIX: IdempotencyWindow.java:43 carries a COUNT of a list that lives in another file, which is the drift vector the commit argues against by name -- it has already drifted once inside a single commit. Stating it as 'some of which DUPLICATE rather than refuse' removes the second copy of the number rather than re-synchronising it.
findings.mutation: no code mutation applies -- this is a prose claim falsified by the staged file itself. Verification performed: three <li> entries in the DUPLICATED <ul> at Sequencer.java:110-137 against 'TWO' at :140 and 'THREE' at IdempotencyWindow.java:43.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader plans a rolling deploy, reaches the closing summary at :139-143 -- the last sentence of the section and the one written to be the takeaway -- counts TWO duplicating cases, checks that neither applies (no pod restart, no v0 checkpoint still in retention) and ships. The third case, the pod absent from an intermediate checkpoint's pods map, needs only two takeovers, which is the deploy they are about to run. The bullet says so at :131-132 and the summary has just told them it is not there. Independently reproduced this round: three leaders, middle leader commits twice at K=1, deltasCarrying(store, 'seg/0') == 2; middle leader commits nothing, == 1; and (discriminating control, new this round) middle leader commits twice at K=1000 so no checkpoint is written, == 1.

findings.summary: the DUPLICATED list's stated derivation no longer covers its own third member -- and the commit's recorded reason says so in as many words
findings.detail: The header reads 'DUPLICATED ... These are what a checkpoint cannot seed'. The third bullet (:125-136) is not that: a checkpoint COULD seed `podb`, and the defect is that the middle leader's checkpoint never RECORDED it. The backlog cell staged in the same commit states the distinction precisely -- 'deriving the family from what a checkpoint cannot SEED missed what a checkpoint does not RECORD' -- so the header is the exact generative rule that was just shown to be incomplete, left standing over the counter-example. This matters more than a wording nit because the commit's own argument is that the list is DERIVED from a rule rather than collected: whoever extends the list next applies the rule as written and will miss the same family again. 'These are what a checkpoint cannot seed OR did not record' is the derivation the evidence supports.
findings.mutation: no code mutation -- falsified by the staged backlog cell's own sentence about the same list.
findings.failure_scenario: The next author extends the list by applying the header's rule -- 'what a checkpoint cannot seed' -- to a new suspected limit, and the third bullet's family (what a checkpoint does not RECORD) is out of scope of that rule, so the same class is missed a second time. That is not hypothetical: it is exactly how the fifth limit was missed at round 1, and the staged backlog cell names the cause in those words.

findings.summary: the recorded reason carries the same stale count: 'two of the four duplicate', over an enumeration the cell itself lists as five
findings.detail: The M5.34 done cell enumerates REFUSED (2) and DUPLICATED (3, naming the fifth limit and M5.55 explicitly), then closes with 'SO THE HEADLINE IS NOT "ANSWERED" AND NOT "ANSWERED OR REFUSED": two of the four duplicate'. Three of five. Same edit as the major finding, one file over; recorded separately because it is the sentence a future reader greps for when the count is questioned again, and because a `done` cell is not swept by any gate.
findings.failure_scenario: The count is questioned a fifth time, someone greps backlog.md for the recorded reason, finds 'two of the four duplicate' in the row whose whole subject is that the count kept being wrong, and now has two disagreeing records of the same enumeration -- one in src/main saying TWO, one in the backlog saying two-of-four, and the list itself holding five.
